_doc: BEN WADE dating cabinet (#20, built 2026-07-18 — completes Tier-1 English except the two web-check brands). THE FOUR-LIVES BRAND, dated by ORIGIN STAMPS: (1) FAMILY ERA Leeds 1860-1965 ('Made in Leeds, England' = hard ceiling 1965 — Lane bought 1962, Leeds factory closed 1965); (2) CHARATAN/LANE SECOND, London Prescott St ~1965-1978 (machine-made; 'Made in London England' or 'London'; pipedia: the 'not earlier than 1973' claim is DISPROVEN by catalogues; Lane heirs sold to Dunhill 1978, Prescott St closed by Mar 1982); (3) ★ DANISH ERA: Preben Holm freehands for Lane, 'Ben Wade Handmade Denmark' 1971-1989 (Feb-1971 Lane-Holm meeting; 1986 downsizing; ended at Holm's death June 1989) — the estate-market cult items; (4) RESURRECTION 1998+: Peter Wilson/Duncan Briars bought the rights from Dunhill, made at the Walthamstow Parker-Hardcastle/Dunhill plant, stamped 'Ben Wade, Made in London, England' AGAIN -> that stamp is TWO-ERA AMBIGUOUS (1965-78 vs 1998+), encoded wide with distinguishers (modern = deep-black blast, ring-grain-suspicious, LASER engraving on latest). SOURCE (local-first): staging/pipedia/Ben_Wade.json (Hacker refs, Valitchka nomenclature gallery, Dreyer collection).

history_anchors._doc: 1860 Benjamin Wade founds the firm in LEEDS, Yorkshire (trader -> 1860s workshop); classic small-dimension English shapes, high grade, no fills. Pre-WWII 3-tier system: 'BEN WADE' top (Larnix, Super Grain, Selected Grain) / 'BW' mid (Statesman, Natural Grain, County) / 'BWL' budget (Hurlingham, Adelphi, Tense Grain, Champion — 2/6 in the 1930s). WWII: Leeds factory DESTROYED by air raids, rebuilt after the war; Champion vanished in the wartime slim-down (name lingers in directories to the early 60s, production unclear). 1962 Lane Ltd (Herman G. Lane, NY) buys Ben Wade AND Charatan; 1965 Leeds factory closed. London machine-made era at Charatan's Prescott Street. 1971: Preben Holm (Copenhagen, in crisis after Snug Harbour default) meets Lane Feb-1971 -> Danish handmade freehand era under the Ben Wade name (whole-page Seven Day's Set ads); huge success; 1986 Holm downsizes; June 1989 Holm dies = third end. 1998: Peter Wilson (Duncan Briars, est. 1899) buys the brand rights from Dunhill -> current Walthamstow production (32 St Andrews Rd — same building+phone as Dunhill pipes). 1890s exemplar: silver-mounted amber-stem cased pipes exist (hallmark-datable via generic router).

brand_marks.physical: Danish-era = hand-carved freehands/fancies (Holm workmanship). Modern (1998+) = deep-black blasts with suspiciously perfect straight/ring grain (rusticated-then-blasted per multiple sources) + LASER-engraved nomenclature on latest production + German vulcanite.

table.note: the FAMILY-ERA stamp — Leeds factory closed 1965 = hard ceiling (Lane ownership from 1962 inside the bracket)
Preben Holm era — Feb-1971 Lane agreement to Holm's death June-1989; the cult freehands

TWO-ERA AMBIGUOUS: Charatan/Lane machine-made 1965-1978 AND the 1998+ Duncan/Wilson resurrection use this stamp (gap 1989-1998 when no Ben Wades were made). Distinguish by build: coarse machine-made + masked fills = 60s-70s London; deep-black perfect-grain blast / laser engraving = 1998+. Never guess between them without features

line_years._notes: Family-tier models -> the Leeds era bracket (1860 wide floor — most are 20th-c; enrichment may tighten). champion: BWL budget line, 2/6 in the 1930s, VANISHED in the WWII slim-down but listed in directories to the early 60s (production unverified) -> honest wide end 1962 with the war story in _doc. special collection: Danish-era freehand (Dreyer exemplar) -> Holm bracket. NOT encoded: super grain (Hardcastle 'Supergrain' collision — cross-brand trap!), county (generic), majestic/prominence/royal grain/reflection/spiral/sitter/matt original (gallery shows them but ERA UNCLEAR — several read Charatan-era, some possibly modern; confirm-flow), seven day sets (Danish-era ads but also generic phrase).
